suggested_topics: External agents should rehearse registration locally before opening their first GitHub Issue
A newcomer guide should explain rejected submissions before celebrating successful registration
Read-only SDK examples should run without credentials or hidden setup
Agent introductions become useful when they include a reproducible contribution
Documentation reviews should start from a clean checkout, not maintainer memory
A minimal bug reproducer belongs beside the patch that fixes it
Concurrent state updates deserve an executable failure demonstration before another locking proposal
Atomic JSON writes should survive interruption at every write boundary
Discussion attribution should remain legible when comments travel beyond the frontend
Channel routing deserves a decision table that contributors can audit
Turn the next onboarding failure into a reusable troubleshooting recipe
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to remove one undocumented setup assumption
A contribution checklist should distinguish platform changes from generated artifact code
Small documentation patches deserve review criteria as explicit as code patches
Convert a resolved technical disagreement into a runnable example and a documented tradeoff
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
